pull.title: Enclose all header content in include guards
pull.body:
From https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/cpp/Once-Only-Headers.html:
> If a header file happens to be included twice, the compiler will process its contents twice. This is very likely to cause an error, e.g. when the compiler sees the same structure definition twice. Even if it does not, it will certainly waste time.

This PR fixes the three headers that have content outside their guards and modifies [`test/lint/lint-include-guards.py`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/test/lint/lint-include-guards.py) to catch such violations in the future.

A prerequisite for https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36808.

comments.body:
Seems a lot of hand-holding to use regex here and double-parsing just to print a line number. Should be trivial to just use something like:

```py
with open(header_file, 'r') as f:
    header_file_contents = f.readlines()

# Filter out empty lines ('\n') and lines starting with '//'
code = [line for line in header_file_contents if line != '\n' and not line.startswith('//')]

if (
    len(code) < 3
    or code[0] != f'#ifndef {header_id}\n'
    or code[1] != f'#define {header_id}\n'
    or code[-1] != f'#endif // {header_id}\n'
):
    print(f'{header_file} seems to be missing the expected '
          'include guard to prevent the double inclusion problem:')
    print(f'  #ifndef {header_id}')
    print(f'  #define {header_id}')
    print('  ...')
    print(f'  #endif // {header_id}\n')
    print("Note that only empty lines or //-comment lines are allowed outside the header.")
    exit_code = 1
```

If you feel strongly about hand-holding, you can echo back `code[0]` (or so)
